svg.title: Figure 4-3. Scene cards: the unsafe control actions of openpilot (C2) (WP-A-05 §4)
svg.desc: One card per UCA of openpilot (C2): UCA-10 openpilot keeps steering while the driver steers against it; UCA-11 openpilot steers out of lane along misleading lines; UCA-12 openpilot stops steering in a curve and says nothing; UCA-13 openpilot holds a stale steering command after the SoC stalls; UCA-14 openpilot accelerates towards a stopped car; UCA-15 openpilot brakes too late for a car cutting in; UCA-16 openpilot brakes hard for nothing; UCA-17 openpilot loses control and the driver is not told; UCA-18 openpilot escalates too slowly when the driver looks away; UCA-19 openpilot and the PCM disagree on engagement; UCA-20 openpilot is set up for the wrong car; UCA-21 openpilot has no assured reaction when the driver stays unresponsive.
svg.text: Figure 4-3. Scene cards: the unsafe control actions of openpilot (C2)

Each card: the UCA type; a road scene (schematic, loops every 6 s); when the control action is needed against what happens; what the controller believes; its control loop with the broken link in red; the loss scenarios and their status.
UCA text and types from WP-A-05 §4, statuses, decisions and requirements from stpa-map.yaml. Scenes and charts explain the scenarios; they are not simulation or test results.

g.title: UCA-10: openpilot keeps steering while the driver steers against it
g.text: FOUR WAYS A CONTROL ACTION GOES WRONG
ROAD SCENE · SCHEMATIC, LOOPS EVERY 6 S
Override seen, but steering torque continues
Pulled back: the car clips the debris
NEEDED WINDOW · WHEN STEERING TORQUE IS WANTED

svg.text: panda limit 1500 raw: no driver-torque term

g.text: “The driver is overriding, but the lane centre
The driver is steering around debris. Steering only overrides;
it never disengages. So openpilot pulls the car back towards
the debris, and the panda passes that torque because its

LS-01 · known gap · inadequate control algorithm

g.title: UCA-11: openpilot steers out of lane along misleading lines
g.text: openpilot steers out of lane along
FOUR WAYS A CONTROL ACTION GOES WRONG
ROAD SCENE · SCHEMATIC, LOOPS EVERY 6 S
Model plans along the old marking
Torque in limits: the panda passes it
NEEDED WINDOW · WHERE THE CAR MUST STAY

svg.text: the driver is the only control

g.text: “The lane bends to the right here.”
Lines are faded and old roadworks markings are left. The model
plans a wrong path, the torque stays inside the envelope, so
the panda passes it. Only the driver can catch it (SOTIF).
CONTROL LOOP · BROKEN LINK IN RED
LS-10 · known gap · inadequate control algorithm

No alert: muted after a steering touch

“The driver touched the wheel, so no warning
The saturation warning needs undershoot, lateral acceleration
and a saturated controller, and is muted for 2 s after any
steering touch. A non-finite target drops steering for a step

g.title: UCA-14: openpilot accelerates towards a stopped car
g.text: FOUR WAYS A CONTROL ACTION GOES WRONG
ROAD SCENE · SCHEMATIC, LOOPS EVERY 6 S
Stopped car ahead; the model misses it
NEEDED WINDOW · WHEN BRAKING IS NEEDED

svg.text: panda bound +2.0 m/s²: knows nothing of leads
needed: brake for the stopped car

g.text: In Chill mode the model can miss a stopped or slower lead. The
planner asks for acceleration, and the panda passes up to +2.0
m/s² because it knows nothing of leads.
CONTROL LOOP · BROKEN LINK IN RED
LS-17 · known gap · inadequate control algorithm

On the Corolla the leads come from the driving model; no radar
is parsed. The same late detection removes planner braking and
CONTROL LOOP · BROKEN LINK IN RED
LS-18 · new finding · inadequate control algorithm

g.title: UCA-16: openpilot brakes hard for nothing
g.text: FOUR WAYS A CONTROL ACTION GOES WRONG
ROAD SCENE · SCHEMATIC, LOOPS EVERY 6 S
The model sees a lead that isn't there
Hard braking; no jerk limit in the panda
NEEDED WINDOW · WHEN BRAKING IS WANTED
A false lead brakes hard. The panda passes any step inside its
bounds and has no jerk limit; the host's jerk limit acts
before pitch compensation and the PID.
CONTROL LOOP · BROKEN LINK IN RED
LS-19 · known gap · inadequate control algorithm

openpilot loses control and the driver

svg.text: needed: alert within the take-over budget
performed: silent; a hung HMI mutes every alert

g.text: “The take-over alert is on the screen and
Every SoC alert goes through ui and soundd, so a hung HMI
mutes them all. The panda's own siren covers only heartbeat

Driver looks away; eyes not seen
Last alert far too late at speed
NEEDED WINDOW · WHEN EACH ALERT IS NEEDED
“The wheel was touched, so the driver is
With low DM confidence the policy falls back to wheel touch:
5, 15 and 25 s, about 750 m at 108 km/h. TSR-634 adds 150, 240
and 395 m, whichever comes first; it is not yet validated on

g.title: UCA-19: openpilot and the PCM disagree on engagement
g.text: openpilot and the PCM disagree on
H-01 unintended steering · H-03 unintended acceleration · H-04 unintended braking · H-07 mode confusion
FOUR WAYS A CONTROL ACTION GOES WRONG
ROAD SCENE · SCHEMATIC, LOOPS EVERY 6 S
Driver presses SET; openpilot not ready
PCM engages cruise, openpilot does not
NEEDED WINDOW · WHEN AUTHORITY MAY STAND

svg.text: until v0.3: granted on the PCM edge

g.text: “I'm not engaged, so I command nothing.”
Until v0.3 the panda granted authority on the PCM's rising
edge whatever openpilot's state. Now it grants only once the
heartbeat says openpilot is engaged (TSR-301), and openpilot
CONTROL LOOP · BROKEN LINK IN RED, SAFETY NET IN GREEN

g.title: UCA-20: openpilot is set up for the wrong car
g.text: openpilot is set up for the wrong car
H-01 unintended steering · H-03 unintended acceleration · H-05 cannot override
FOUR WAYS A CONTROL ACTION GOES WRONG
ROAD SCENE · SCHEMATIC, LOOPS EVERY 6 S
Panda lock passes: the parameter matches
Host tuning wrong: the car weaves
NEEDED WINDOW · HOW WELL THE CAR MUST TRACK
A wrong brand or parameter leaves the panda in NOOUTPUT, so
engagement is refused. Another Toyota with EPS scale 73 and no
flags gets the same parameter: the envelope is right, the host
CONTROL LOOP · BROKEN LINK IN RED

g.title: UCA-21: openpilot has no assured reaction when the driver stays unresponsive
g.text: UCA-21 · OPENPILOT (C2) · TYPE N, NOT PROVIDED
openpilot has no assured reaction when
FOUR WAYS A CONTROL ACTION GOES WRONG
ROAD SCENE · SCHEMATIC, LOOPS EVERY 6 S
5 s later the car brakes to a stop
No announcement, no hazard lights, hold not proven
NEEDED WINDOW · WHAT THE REACTION MUST INCLUDE
“The driver will respond to the alerts.”
After alert 3 and 5 s more, the car brakes to a stop in its
lane. Missing: an announcement, hazard lights, an assured hold
and a lockout until the driver responds (DQ-365, TSR-633).
CONTROL LOOP · BROKEN LINK IN RED
LS-35 · known gap · inadequate control algorithm
